gap: No result ChatGPT got that I could open states how much card each pick fills with all three cameras recording: by DashCamTalk's per-channel bitrates the "2K" VIOFO A229 Plus 3CH writes about 30.6 GB an hour, more than the "4K" Vantrue N4 Pro S (about 25.1 GB) or the N4S (about 20.0 GB), so a 256 GB card loops after roughly 8.4, 10.2 and 12.8 hours.
standout_why: Compared against Product Bible's best-3-channel page only (opened 2026-11-21). It gives resolution, frame rate, sensor and maximum card size per model, but no bitrates, no hours per card and no per-channel HDR, and it says outright that it has no separate figures for 3-channel mode. It already notes that Vantrue's "2.5K" rear is 1440p, so the naming point is only partly new. I could not read the other two cited pages: vortexradar.com/best-dashcams returned HTTP 403 and ezdashcam.com/collections/under-300 returned HTTP 429. Vortex Radar may discuss bitrates, so the score could be 1 once that page is read.
decides: It confirms the pick rather than changing it. The Vantrue N4 Pro S fits under $300 for the camera alone, and its 1 TB card limit against the A229 Plus's 512 GB gives it about 40 hours of three-camera footage against about 17 at maximum card size. The N4S is the only one of the three DashCamTalk lists with HDR on all three cameras, and it writes the least per hour, which supports it as the value pick. Bitrate here is a card-size figure, not a detail ranking: the DashCamTalk pages I read did not give the codec for each camera. Every maker store was rate-limited today, so the page's deciding spec (resolution and frame rate per channel in 3-channel mode from the maker's page or manual) and the hardwire-kit prices still have to be read before publishing.

findings.label: Per-channel resolution, frame rate, sensor and average bitrate (DashCamTalk spec sheet)
findings.value: Front 3840 × 2160, 30 fps, IMX678, 32.0 Mbps; rear 2560 × 1440, 30 fps, IMX675, 14.0 Mbps; cabin 1080p, 30 fps, IMX662, 9.8 Mbps
findings.note: 3-channel: front, cabin (4 IR LEDs), rear. DashCamTalk's figures; the page gives no list of resolution combinations by recording mode.

findings.label: Card use with all three cameras recording (derived)
findings.value: 55.8 Mbps total = about 25.1 GB per hour; about 10.2 hours on a 256 GB card, about 39.8 hours on the 1 TB maximum
findings.note: Arithmetic: 32.0 + 14.0 + 9.8 = 55.8 Mbps; × 3600 s ÷ 8 ÷ 1000 = 25.11 GB/h; 256 ÷ 25.11 = 10.2 h; 1000 ÷ 25.11 = 39.8 h. Decimal GB, video bitrate only, before formatting overhead and locked event files.

findings.label: HDR by channel (DashCamTalk)
findings.value: Front: yes, set manually; rear: no; cabin: not listed
findings.note: ChatGPT's table said "STARVIS 2: all 3"; the sensor is on all three but DashCamTalk lists HDR on the front only.

findings.label: Parking mode, storage, heat (DashCamTalk)
findings.value: Buffered motion detection, collision detection, low-bitrate and low-frame-rate parking modes, all needing the optional hardwire kit; microSD up to 1 TB; capacitor; -20 °C to 65 °C
findings.note: DashCamTalk adds that collision detection is "not useful as recording starts 10+ seconds after impact". Product Bible quotes the manual at -20 °C to 60 °C, so the upper limit differs between the two.

findings.label: Price on DashCamTalk's tracker, dated 2026-11-21
findings.note: A third-party tracker, not a store read: vantrue.com returned HTTP 429 to the page fetch and to storecheck.py today. It matches the $279.99 in our record (read 2026-11-14).

findings.label: What the box price leaves out (Notebookcheck, Stephen Pereyra)
findings.value: The $419.00 base price excludes the hardwire kit, the SD card and the filter; microSD up to 1 TB
findings.source_title: Vantrue N4 Pro S Review - Notebookcheck
findings.note: Review published 2025-11-22, updated 2026-10-05. It confirms 2160p front (IMX678), 1080p cabin (IMX662), 1440p rear (IMX675) at 30 fps, and gives no hardwire-kit price.

findings.label: Per-channel resolution, frame rate, sensor and average bitrate (DashCamTalk)
findings.value: Front 2560 × 1440, 30 fps, IMX675, 29 Mbps; rear 2560 × 1440, 30 fps, IMX675, 24 Mbps; cabin 1080p, 30 fps, IMX307 (first-generation STARVIS), 15 Mbps
findings.note: 3-channel: front, cabin, rear. HDR: front yes (scheduled), rear no, cabin not stated. The page gives no differences by channel count.

findings.label: Card use with all three cameras recording (derived)
findings.value: 68 Mbps total = about 30.6 GB per hour; about 8.4 hours on a 256 GB card, about 16.7 hours on the 512 GB maximum
findings.note: Arithmetic: 29 + 24 + 15 = 68 Mbps; × 3600 ÷ 8 ÷ 1000 = 30.6 GB/h; 256 ÷ 30.6 = 8.4 h; 512 ÷ 30.6 = 16.7 h. Same basis as the Vantrue rows.

findings.label: Parking mode, storage, heat (DashCamTalk)
findings.value: Buffered auto event detection, time-lapse and low-bitrate parking modes, needing a hardwire (DashCamTalk recommends VIOFO's 3-wire kit with low-voltage cutoff); microSD up to 512 GB; capacitor; -10 °C to 65 °C

findings.label: Per-channel resolution, frame rate, sensor and bitrate (DashCamTalk)
findings.value: Front, rear and cabin each listed at 2560 × 1440, 30 fps, IMX675, 14.8 Mbps, with scheduled HDR on all three
findings.note: 3-channel: front, cabin, rear. Forum reviewers quoted on the same page give front-only 2592 × 1944 at 30 fps and 3-channel "1944P+1440P+1440P 30FPS", which matches Product Bible's 1944p front. So the front is 2592 × 1944 by those accounts, not the table's 2560 × 1440. The page does not say whether 14.8 Mbps is an average.

findings.label: Card use with all three cameras recording (derived)
findings.value: 44.4 Mbps total = about 20.0 GB per hour; about 12.8 hours on a 256 GB card, about 50 hours on the 1 TB maximum
findings.note: Arithmetic: 14.8 × 3 = 44.4 Mbps; × 3600 ÷ 8 ÷ 1000 = 19.98 GB/h; 256 ÷ 19.98 = 12.8 h; 1000 ÷ 19.98 = 50.1 h. Other specs on the page: buffered, time-lapse and low-bitrate parking modes; capacitor; -20 °C to 60 °C.

findings.label: Price on DashCamTalk's tracker, dated 2026-11-21
findings.note: A third-party tracker, not a store read. It matches the $199.99 in the brief's partner table for the Nexus 4S (read 2026-11-21) and explains ChatGPT's two prices ($209.99 Best Buy card, $199.99 "recently reported").

findings.label: The table footnote: same rear sensor and pixel count, different data rate
findings.value: The rear cameras of the N4 Pro S (Vantrue calls it "2.5K") and the A229 Plus (VIOFO calls it "2K") are both 2560 × 1440 at 30 fps on an IMX675; DashCamTalk lists 24 Mbps for VIOFO's and 14.0 Mbps for Vantrue's, about 71% more data for the same pixels
findings.note: 24 ÷ 14.0 = 1.71. Vantrue figure from https://dashcamtalk.com/vantrue-n4-pro-s/ (read 2026-11-21). Per pixel per frame: A229 Plus front 0.26, rear 0.22 bits; N4 Pro S front 0.13, rear 0.13 bits (bitrate ÷ (width × height × 30)). The codec for each camera was not on the pages read, so use this for card sizing, not as a detail ranking. ChatGPT's first table showed "2.5K" against "2K" as if they differed.

findings.label: What the cited Product Bible page already has
findings.value: Per-model resolution and fps (N4 Pro S 4K/1440p/1080p at 30 fps; N4S 1944p/1440p/1440p; A229 Pro 3CH 4K/2K/1080p at $299.99), sensors and maximum card size; no bitrates, no hours per card, no hardwire-kit prices, no per-mode resolution
findings.source_title: Best 3-Channel Dash Cams With Interior Camera (2026) | Product Bible
findings.note: Its prices are dated 2026-11-19. It does not cover the A229 Plus 3CH. It lists the A229 Pro 3CH cabin sensor as a first-generation IMX307.
